title: Exploration experience and new alliance partners
x: Accumulated structure-exploration experience through preceding year: historical average indicator that alliance partner had no prior joint alliance
y: Current-year structure exploration: average new-partner indicator over alliances formed that year
timeHorizon: The current calendar year, with experience measured through the preceding year
setting: A public US software firm forms alliances during a calendar year. Its historical structure-exploration experience is the share of earlier alliances formed with partners that were new at the time. Current structure exploration is the share of current-year alliances with previously unallied partners. Total past alliance count is comparable across the experience-composition contrast.
task: Rate how greater accumulated experience with new partners changes the proportion of current-year alliances formed with new partners. Compare lower X (Lower historical proportion of alliances with previously unallied partners) with higher X (Higher historical proportion of alliances with previously unallied partners). Use the same X contrast in both contexts. A positive rating means higher X is associated with more Y; a negative rating means less Y. Rate the relationship, not the overall level of Y. Do not interpret this judgment as a measured empirical coefficient.

xContrast.lower: Lower historical proportion of alliances with previously unallied partners
xContrast.higher: Higher historical proportion of alliances with previously unallied partners

sharedFacts: The outcome is an annual proportion of alliances with new partners, not a choice between two named partners.
The historical-experience contrast concerns its composition, not its volume, success, or experience with one particular candidate.

sourceEvidence.citation: Lavie, D., and Rosenkopf, L. (2006). Balancing Exploration and Exploitation in Alliance Formation. Academy of Management Journal, 49(4), 797-818.
sourceEvidence.measurementNotes: Public US software firms; same total partnering experience, function and attribute conditions
sourceEvidence.translationNotes: General partnering experience is a separate control. Do not interpret experience as success or ties with one candidate. Historical indicator is evaluated at each alliance date. Annual averages do not identify a single randomized partner choice.
